items.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001
items.q: I love him. And I can listen to him any mood at any time. ... while Art Tatum had it, he would kind of venture off of it ... But then later on, as you get to know the piano better, he is totally amazing.

ctx.x: It was very weird. They didn’t have really schools that much. There was one school called the Westlake College of Music. And my parents took me there when I was fourteen and I remember studying a little bit with a piano player named Dave Robertson and also one named Gene Garf. And I remember Gene Garf liked Art Tatum a lot and I didn’t at that time. And they would give me a tune a week or something, I would learn a tune, and it would be a standard. They didn’t say anything and it really, there was no way that you…

be G flat. But you know the funny thing about not knowing anything too much and not having many teachers was that I didn’t know that was hard, or I didn’t think too much, it was just something I really liked to do. And I thought that the feeling of the music was incredible. I still feel that way when I hear Bird and Bud. Nothing left. So those two are really amazing. A lot of times you hear music, of course I have a different opinion of Art Tatum, I love him now too. But sometimes you know you hear music and it…
